leaders.notes: Fifth president of Gannon; oversaw major fundraising and campus renovation. Resigned in May 2000; later became the subject of a Title IX retaliation lawsuit (Petruska v. Gannon University) and posthumous sexual-misconduct allegations surfaced publicly years afterward.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Longtime Gannon faculty member (Political Science, 25 years) who moved from provost to acting president during the search that produced Garibaldi.

Sixth president; led 24% enrollment growth and a $31.5M campaign. Left in 2010 to become the 25th president (first lay and first African American president) of University of Detroit Mercy, serving there 2011-2022.

Named interim president effective Jan. 1, 2011, after Garibaldi's departure; served roughly six months while the university completed its search for a permanent president. Not a candidate for the permanent role.

Seventh president; served twelve years, reorganized academic structure and opened a Ruskin, FL satellite campus. Stepped down effective June 2023 citing a planned life/family transition; became Gannon's first President Emeritus.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Student Experience
leaders.notes: Eighth and current president, began July 1, 2023; previously chief academic officer and then provost at Gannon.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President of Academic and Student Affairs
leaders.notes: Tenth president, in office since 1986 (predates the 1996 window but included since his term ran through 2002). Resigned in October 2002 amid a grading/athletics scandal that also led the NCAA to place the university on three years' probation.
Served as interim president following White's resignation until A. Frank Bonner was named the permanent 12th president in 2005; exact prior/subsequent roles not confirmed in available sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President (formerly VP for Academic and Student Affairs)
leaders.notes: 12th president, took office July 1, 2005 after nearly 14 years as president; had joined Gardner-Webb in 1987 as VP for Academic Affairs. Announced retirement in January 2019.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Thomas Harriot College of Arts and Sciences
leaders.notes: 13th president, took office 2019; oversaw several capital projects. Resigned effective Feb. 18, 2025 to become president of Campbell University (NC), starting there in July 2025.

Began as interim president in February 2025 upon Downs' departure, then was appointed the permanent 14th president effective November 11, 2025. U.S. Air Force veteran; previously VP for Advancement at Gardner-Webb and a senior advancement officer at East Carolina University.

10th president. Suffered a stroke caused by a brain tumor in June 1997 and died in 1998; sources vary on whether his presidency is formally listed as ending in 1997 or 1998 (used here since Brandt's presidency began Aug. 1998, immediately after).
11th president, took office Aug. 1, 1998. Announced retirement in October 2006, effective 2007; George Fox's Brandt Hall residence is named for him.
12th and current president, effective July 1, 2007; had served eight years as provost overseeing academic expansion. Began career as a history professor at Wheaton College.

leaders.priorTitle: Provincial, Maryland Province of the Society of Jesus
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: University of Massachusetts Boston (acting provost), then John Carroll University (president, 1998-2005)
leaders.notes: Ousted/resigned under board pressure in May 1997 after a brief, contentious tenure. Went on to serve as president of John Carroll University from 1998-2005.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Administration and Planning
leaders.nextRole: Vice President for Administration and Planning
leaders.notes: The only non-Jesuit to serve as Gonzaga's president; stepped in as acting president during a period of financial and enrollment difficulty, then returned to his VP role until his death.

leaders.priorTitle: Associate Professor of Philosophy / Frank Shrontz Chair of Professional Ethics
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Magis Center (and Spitzer Center of Ethical Leadership)
leaders.notes: 25th president, inaugurated Sept. 17, 1998; led major campus expansion (20 new facilities) and a $200M+ capital/scholarship campaign. Left in 2009 to found the Magis Center, a faith-and-reason institute.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Administration and Planning / Interim Academic Vice President
leaders.notes: Named interim successor to Spitzer on July 15, 2009, then confirmed as the 26th (first lay) president in 2010. Announced retirement in April 2024, effective July 14, 2025; named Gonzaga's first president emeritus.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice President (with a year as interim president)
leaders.notes: 27th and current president, took office July 15, 2025; the first woman to lead Gonzaga in its 137-year history. Earlier career included dean/distinguished chair roles at St. John's University and dean of the Honors College at NJIT.
